title: Keep WebGPU selected and remove automatic Canvas fallbacks
description: Prevents automatic Canvas rendering when WebGPU is selected, ensuring that unsupported scenes display an error until GPU support is fixed or the user explicitly selects Canvas.
body:
Selecting WebGPU currently lets initialization failures, unsupported geometry, GPU device loss, or older X-Ray support silently mount the Canvas renderer. A board with unsupported breakout-point metadata can therefore enter the expensive Canvas path despite WebGPU being selected.

Keep WebGPU selected throughout these cases. Display the renderer failure and release its worker, or show an unsupported-X-Ray notice while retaining the GPU view. Canvas remains available through an explicit rendering-engine selection. Also use an event listener for worker message errors and prevent duplicate worker termination after failure.

Update the documentation and integration checks to assert that failures never mount Canvas, failed workers are released, manual Canvas selection still works, and unsupported X-Ray keeps the GPU canvas visible.

Validation:
- `bun run build` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Built-bundle browser checks via the in-app browser passed for unavailable WebGPU, unsupported geometry, worker errors, message errors, simulated device loss, startup timeout, unsupported X-Ray, and explicit Canvas selection after failure.
- The automated WebGPU runner was updated but not executed locally; its large-board performance and StrictMode checks remain unverified in this run.

This prevents automatic Canvas rendering; unsupported scenes now show an error until their GPU support is fixed or the user explicitly selects Canvas. It does not establish that every cause of the reported Chrome hang has been resolved.

title: Add source_runtime_error for circuit generation failures
description: Add source_runtime_error to represent an unexpected failure while generating or validating a circuit, allowing consumers to distinguish incomplete validation from a clean circuit.
body:
A DRC checker can throw before returning its design-rule diagnostics. Consumers currently cannot distinguish incomplete validation from a clean circuit by inspecting Circuit JSON.

Add `source_runtime_error` to represent an unexpected failure while generating or validating a circuit, with only required `message` and optional `phase_name` beyond the standard type, ID, and error_type fields. This is distinct from a design-rule violation. Export the schema/input/interface and register it in `any_circuit_element`.

Validation: all 397 tests pass; package build and TypeScript check pass. The new test verifies JSON round-trip through the union and required message and optional phase.

Core will use this to preserve a rendered circuit and successful DRC results while serializing failed check groups. This complements https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5018, which guards against unreported asynchronous failures.

title: Infer pin 1 orientation for numbered straight pad rows
description: Extends the existing analyzers two-pad convention to infer pin 1 orientation for longer straight pad rows with unique, consecutive pin numbers, resolving supplier placement preparation failures.
body:
`analyzePcbPin1Location` could infer a canonical orientation for a two-pad line, but returned null for longer straight rows. A routed JST PH J1 has pins 1–4 from -X to +X, while JLCPCB C131334 runs from +X to -X. The missing orientation caused supplier placement preparation to fail and let a permissive PnP export keep 90° instead of the needed 270°.

Extend the existing analyzer's two-pad convention to straight rows with unique, consecutive pin numbers in physical order. This lets the authored and supplier footprints compare consistently and reveals the 180° reversal. Ambiguous or nonmonotonic rows remain unresolved; other multi-row footprints keep the existing behavior. The fix uses plated-hole pad geometry, not CAD model rotation or a part-specific offset.

Tests cover the actual J1 and C131334 pad coordinates, all right-angle combinations, and ambiguous numbering. Validation: `bun test` (139 passing, 599 assertions, 4 snapshots), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check` pass. All GitHub checks pass. The package manifest has one formatting-only change because the repository-wide format check rejected its existing array layout.

This shared analyzer change supersedes the closed [PnP PR #22](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-pnp-csv/pull/22). After release, the PnP package needs to update its utility dependency and retain a J1 regression. The CLI export path also needs to prepare supplier orientation metadata for prebuilt Circuit JSON.

title: Add schSize to diode and LED props
description: Adds schSize to diode and LED props using the existing SchematicSymbolSize API, enabling typed JSX for compact symbols.
body:
Adds `schSize` to diode and LED props using the existing `SchematicSymbolSize` API. This enables typed JSX such as `<diode schSize="sm" />`, `<diode zener schSize="xs" />`, and `<led schSize="sm" />` for the compact symbols introduced in tscircuit/schematic-symbols#483.

The prop is optional, with no new default or aliases. It accepts `sm`, `xs`, `default`, `md`, and existing distance inputs. Named sizes are preserved; distance inputs normalize to millimeters. Also checks named sizes before distance parsing and rejects nonfinite results, preventing the shared schema from turning `sm` into NaN with older circuit-json versions.

Generated component types and documentation are updated. Validation: all 568 tests, package build, TypeScript, and formatting pass. Core symbol selection is implemented in the dependent draft https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4216.

title: Reproduce USB-C shell pad ambiguity with snapshots
description: Reproduces a bug where duplicate USB-C shell pins lose their PCB connections despite being wired to a ground header in the schematic.
body:
### Motivation
- Show duplicate USB-C shell pins losing their PCB connections despite being wired to a ground header in the schematic.

### Before
- The snapshots had no external ground header or enabled routing, making the missing copper connection difficult to see.

### After
- Use self-contained TSX with four shell slots, explicit wires and local routing. No JSON fixture is needed. The schematic shows the ground connection while the PCB snapshot has no routed traces.
- Verified the failure before the fix and two routed traces with the fix. The diagnostic test is skipped after generating the failure snapshots so the stacked code-only fix can inherit the same repro files.

title: fix: preserve rotated plated-hole obstacles in SRJ
description: Fixes incorrect dimensions of rotated rectangular plated-hole obstacles in SRJ by ensuring proper rotation is applied during obstacle generation.
body:
## Summary

- route `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` through Core's existing rotation-aware rectangular plated-hole obstacle conversion
- preserve correct SRJ dimensions for quarter-turn pads and rotation for non-axis-aligned pads
- add a TSX repro using the exact PMP23595 T500-T503 pad geometry at 90° and 270°

## Root cause

Circuit JSON correctly retained `rect_ccw_rotation`, but `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` handled circular holes with rectangular pads in a separate branch that copied `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height` without applying that rotation. On PMP23595, this changed each `12.7 × 17.272 mm` board-space pad obstacle into `17.272 × 12.7 mm`, making the two real routing gaps appear overlapped in SRJ.

The fix removes that unrotated special case and reuses the same established rotated-rectangle path as the other rectangular plated-hole variants.

![PMP23595 rotated rectangular plated-hole repro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/fix/rotated-rect-plated-hole-obstacles/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-pmp23595-rotated-rect-pad-srj-obstacles-pcb.snap.svg)

## Verification

- PMP23595 repro asserts `12.7 × 17.272 mm` SRJ obstacles at both 90° and 270°
- repro asserts the original `4.4196 mm` and `3.6068 mm` gaps
- related rotated SMT-pad, plated-slot, copper-pour, and plated-hole tests pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Refresh cached supplier pin 1 orientation for straight-row connectors
description: Updates the cached supplier pin 1 orientation for straight-row connectors by advancing the cache key and updating the dependency to ensure correct orientation is computed.
body:
Core already calls `analyzePcbPin1Location`, but its installed `circuit-json-util` version predates the four-pin straight-row fix. A prior build may also have cached JLC C131334's orientation as `null`, so updating the dependency alone would leave J1 unresolved.

Update Core to `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util@^0.0.117` and advance the supplier orientation cache key from v3 to v4. This makes Core recompute the JST PH pin-1 locations: the authored footprint has pin 1 on the left, while JLC's C131334 footprint has pin 1 on the right. The renderer's geometry and the analyzer implementation stay in their existing packages.

Validation: focused orientation tests (5 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run build`, and Biome checks pass. A new PCB snapshot test seeds the stale v3 `null` result and verifies that a second render reuses the v4 result.

title: Serialize DRC execution failures in circuit JSON
description: Serializes DRC execution failures in Circuit JSON, ensuring that diagnostics from successful checks are preserved and failures are logged without disrupting the rendering of the circuit.
body:
When a DRC check rejects, the renderer currently logs the exception and settles without a Circuit JSON error. `Promise.all` also discards diagnostics from successful check groups. A copper-pour boundary-operation exception in the smart-ring benchmark therefore produced a successful CLI build with incomplete DRC.

Group Board, its interface, and its helpers under `normal-components/Board/` and update all import paths. Move DRC scheduling and execution into `Board/Board_updatePcbDesignRuleChecks.ts`, following the existing Board helper pattern. `Board.updatePcbDesignRuleChecks()` delegates to that helper.

Catch execution failures per check group and insert a `source_runtime_error` containing `phase_name` and `message`. The message includes the check identity and exception text. Defer check invocation so synchronous throws are handled too. Successful groups still contribute diagnostics, the rendered circuit remains available, and repeated settling does not duplicate failures or rerun the checks.

Uses published `circuit-json@0.0.507`, including the merged source_runtime_error schema from https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/844. Updates both the dev dependency and override; this repository does not track a dependency lockfile.

Validation against the published package:
- 31 DRC, fabricator, and Board lifecycle tests pass, including both runtime-failure regressions.
- TypeScript check passes.
- The regression tests verify serialization, preserved PCB components and successful diagnostics, synchronous and asynchronous failures, non-Error rejections, and no duplicate errors after settling twice.

Failures are isolated at the check-group API boundary. If `runAllRoutingChecks` aborts before returning, results internal to that failed group cannot be recovered here. This does not fix the underlying copper-pour geometry exception.

Related CLI safeguard: https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5018. Handled DRC failures now appear in Circuit JSON for normal build diagnostics; the safeguard still covers other unhandled asynchronous render failures.

title: fix: convert outline keepouts to SRJ obstacles
description: Fixes the issue where outline keepouts were not being converted to SRJ obstacles in the circuit JSON model, ensuring proper rendering and obstacle generation.
body:
Stacked on #4207.

## Root fix

Circuit JSON models a stroked keepout path as `pcb_keepout` with `shape: "outline"`, but `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` only consumed circle and rectangle keepouts. This adds the missing shape conversion at that contract boundary.

Outline keepouts are rendered with round caps and joins. The conversion therefore decomposes the stroke using the existing obstacle approximation utilities:

- `generateApproximatingRects` approximates each rotated segment body
- `fillCircleWithRects` approximates the round join/cap at each unique vertex

The resulting obstacles are axis-aligned SRJ rectangles, preserve the source layers, have no electrical connectivity, and use stable keepout/segment/join-derived IDs.

There is no board-specific circle detection, expanded segment length, custom rectangle approximation, renderer compensation, custom SRJ shape, or connectivity inference.

## Real-board result

The real TI TMDS62LEVM crop now passes. Its 2.17779854 mm rounded keepout is visibly larger than the enclosed 1.00000054 mm pad obstacle and the SRJ approximation preserves the source shape.

The 48 segment bodies produce 96 rectangles through `generateApproximatingRects`. The 48 unique round joins produce 192 rectangles through `fillCircleWithRects`. The right panel contains only the resulting SRJ rectangles; it has no synthetic circle or source overlay.

![TMDS62LEVM real-board outline keepout SRJ obstacles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/9b68021466b7f6d1589eaa64a0536b22b0fc1888/tests/repros/__snapshots__/ti-tmds62levm-outline-keepout-obstacle.snap.svg)

## User-facing TSX reproduction

This PR reproduces the issue through the public API a Core user uses: a real TSX board rendered and routed by Core's default autorouter. It does not import a Circuit JSON fixture, call `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` directly, or replace routing with a capture stub.

The circuit mirrors the PMP23653 planar-transformer connector topology:

- `J5` and `J7`: 12 physical terminals on `net.SECONDARY`
- `J3`: 6 physical terminals on `net.PRIMARY`
- two multi-terminal `<trace path={...}>` elements, each attached to its named net

The circuit has two electrical nets and two source traces. Current Core submits four routing jobs: one trace-owned and one net-owned connection for each identical endpoint group.

## What the default router proves

```text
SECONDARY source trace + SECONDARY source net -> 2 input jobs for the same 12 pads
PRIMARY   source trace + PRIMARY   source net -> 2 input jobs for the same  6 pads
```

The default solver merges the identical endpoint groups and emits 16 physical route segments, so the final PCB view alone hides the redundant input. The autorouting phase snapshot exposes the real defect: **4 submitted connections for 2 electrical nets**. Its routed output is associated with the two trace-owned jobs.

title: fix: enforce via-in-pad restrictions using hole overlap for all nets
description: Fixes via placement errors by enforcing restrictions on same-net vias whose drilled holes enter a pad when via-in-pad is disallowed, ensuring proper error reporting for overlapping vias.
body:
A same-net via whose drilled hole enters a pad must report a placement error when `is_via_in_pad_allowed` is false or omitted. Explicit `true` continues to allow it. Copper-ring contact alone no longer counts as via-in-pad.

The check measures the circular drill against the pad outline on shared layers. Full enclosure and partial drill intrusion report an error; external drill tangency and copper-only contact do not. Different-net copper overlap remains a violation in `checkViaPadClearance`, including when via-in-pad is enabled.

Builds on the reproduction merged in #358. Both branches retain separate allowed/disallowed TSX tests and SVG snapshots. The disallowed test changes from the incorrect empty result to the actual placement error; the allowed control remains unchanged. An additional TSX/SVG fixture shows eight positions across the pad edge, and unit tests cover the boundary and curved, rotated, and polygon pads. The Game Boy fixture retains all 11 copper-clearance errors but no longer misclassifies its five copper-only overlaps as via-in-pad.

[JLCPCB's guide](https://jlcpcb.com/blog/via-in-pad-in-pcb) describes vias inside component soldering pads and recommends full encapsulation by metal-defined pads. Its [BGA guidance](https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/bga-design-guidelines---pcb-layout-recommendations-for-bga-packages) distinguishes drill-to-pad spacing from copper-to-pad spacing. These sources do not specify an exact partial-overlap classification algorithm: counting partial drill intrusion is a conservative DRC choice, not a claim to reproduce JLCPCB's internal DFM.

![Same-net vias across a pad edge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/checks/4e51fda554c8235f548bc53241159d4a6726d421/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-same-net-via-at-pad-edge.snap.svg)

title: Fix false SVG outages from cold-render timeouts
description: Fixes false SVG outages by increasing the timeout for cold-render requests to 15 seconds and improving SVG content validation.
body:
The SVG monitor marks healthy cold renders as outages because it allows only five seconds. Actual PCB/schematic requests from GitHub Actions returned valid images in 6.3–7.6 seconds; the previous Node deployment also exceeded the threshold (5.4–6.2 seconds). Warm current-production requests completed in 1.1–1.3 seconds.

Allow 15 seconds for each complete image response, disable redundant ky retries (the runner already retries), and verify SVG content and successful-render headers. Include the failing view, elapsed time, and error in status failures. Add unit coverage and a PR workflow that requests actual production PCB/schematic images.

Validation: four unit tests and TypeScript checks pass locally. [Cold production reproduction](https://github.com/tscircuit/status/actions/runs/36673566378), [comparison with previous Node deployment](https://github.com/tscircuit/status/actions/runs/36673666365). Temporary diagnostic scripts/workflows were removed from the final diff. No dependency patches or runtime rollback.

Updates the rendering stack using `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.229`, which includes the upstream Node compatibility fix from tscircuit/checks#362. The published checks bundle no longer leaks the `calculate-elbow/lib` directory import that caused production requests to fail despite successful builds. No checks postinstall patch or direct calculate-elbow workaround is used; the existing OCCT/fanout patch script is unchanged.

Updates core/eval/props/tscircuit, circuit-to-svg, common, ngspice, snippet URLs, 3D PNG rendering, React, and supporting libraries. Reviews and refreshes the affected 2D snapshots and adds an endpoint regression test for automatic PCB teardrops and disabling one end. Existing 3D snapshots and the exact JLCPCB SVG hash assertion remain unchanged.

Three compatibility holds keep this update safe:
- `biscuitboard@1.0.10`: newer releases remove `Clad40x40`, breaking existing board code.
- `@tscircuit/fanout-solver@0.0.46`: newer 0.0.78 fails Vercel type checking in `complete-original-endpoints.ts` (`string | undefined` returned as `string`).
- `circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.118`: newer conversion loses visible lead detail in the vectorized JLCPCB preview. Retaining this version restores the exact original SVG hash.

Next.js, TypeScript, Biome, and vectorizer major/minor migrations remain separate work. This PR does not update every dependency to latest.

Validation:
- Local production build, production Node smoke test, formatting, and full suite: **59 passed, 0 failed**.
- Production smoke coverage inherited from #2398 exercises cold health, code evaluation/routing, PCB/schematic/assembly SVG and PNG, 3D PNG, repeat rendering, and the legacy Biscuit Board fixture.
- Linux CI: build, formatting, Node 22 production smoke, and full test job all pass on `7adfdad2bf6150d50f8dc081d5990a31f34cfb63`.
- Vercel deployment succeeds and every production smoke check passes against the [immutable preview](https://svg-tscircuit-jsgy70iac-tscircuit.vercel.app), including 3D PNG and the legacy Biscuit Board fixture.

title: Use Bun on Vercel and align rendering dependencies with tscircuit
description: Moves Vercel functions to Bun using bunVersion: 1.x and upgrades the rendering stack to current tscircuit versions, ensuring compatibility and improved performance.
body:
Moves Vercel functions to Bun using `bunVersion: "1.x"` and upgrades the rendering stack to current tscircuit versions. Builds and CI use Bun 1.3.14, frozen installs, Next.js 16.3.7, and Biome 2.5.14. The uncached health response exposes `X-Runtime` so deployed smoke tests verify that requests actually execute on Bun. Node fallback smoke coverage remains in the required test job.

Dependency alignment:
- `tscircuit@0.0.2679`, `@tscircuit/core@0.0.2016`, and `@tscircuit/eval@0.0.1491` match the current upstream release.
- Updates fanout-solver from 0.0.46 to upstream's 0.0.78, GLTF from 0.0.118 to 0.0.134, and vectorizer from 0.0.5 to 0.1.0. Retains the published checks fix at 0.0.229.
- Updates Biscuit Board to 1.0.28 and removes obsolete `Clad40x40` compatibility checks. TypeScript remains 5.9.3 to match tscircuit's 5.x peer requirement.
- Overrides poppygl to 0.0.29, matching tscircuit and the latest published release. This removes the renderer-local 0.0.24 copy allowed by circuit-json-to-3d-png's dependency range. A regression test verifies the version resolved from inside the renderer matches both the override and tscircuit.

The updated GLTF renderer changes the board and trace colors. The previous vectorization noise filter also discarded fine-pitch IC leads; lowering its filtering preserves those details without dependency patches. Reviewed and refreshed the 3D snapshots and exact JLCPCB SVG hash; test thresholds are unchanged. The existing OCCT/fanout postinstall patches are unchanged, with no new patches introduced.

Next.js configuration moves file tracing out of `experimental`, keeps webpack for the existing build, and includes the generated TypeScript updates. Biome's configuration is migrated and excludes generated `next-env.d.ts` from formatting.

Vercel installs into a clean `node_modules` directory before its frozen install: restoring the previous deployment cache otherwise retained an obsolete renderer-local poppygl copy. Every build runs the renderer-resolution regression test before compiling, so stale copies fail the build.

Validation on `3e5a092f5dd979d48d23131060bd333e0af7ef98`:
- All required GitHub checks pass: build, formatting, Bun and Node production smoke, and the full test suite.
- Local full suite: **60 tests / 0 failures**, snapshot updating disabled.
- The [immutable Vercel preview](https://svg-tscircuit-vcz2t2vgy-tscircuit.vercel.app) reports `X-Runtime: bun` and passes cold health, code evaluation/routing, PCB/schematic/assembly SVG and PNG, 3D PNG and SVG, and repeat rendering.
- The deployed JLCPCB fine-pitch chip SVG matches the reviewed poppygl 0.0.29 output's exact SHA-256 hash (`3161a299152768b84688e2879f17780f5e5faac56a89fcddb5c4b738052d3302`).
- Updated 3D snapshots were visually reviewed with component geometry and fine-pitch leads preserved. Test thresholds are unchanged.

Vercel manages the runtime version within its [Bun 1.x line](https://vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes/bun), currently 1.3.14. Bun 1.4 is not selected. Ready for review; auto-merge is not enabled.

title: Improve Pipeline 9 clearance repair for straight trace spans
description: Long, straight trace spans can remain too close to copper because the clearance projector only moves existing vertices and their endpoints are locked. body: Long, straight trace spans can remain too close to copper because the clearance projector only moves existing vertices and their endpoints are locked. Add bounded subdivisions to constant-width spans on routes implicated in DRC errors, then run a refinement pass after the existing independent wire repairs. This gives the solver nearby vertices to bend while retaining terminals, junctions, widths, and via sites. The change is in Pipeline 9's clearance-repair logic and applies to any eligible input. It contains no fixture-specific conditions, error filtering, changed DRC thresholds, or solver-failure suppression. Existing changed-segment collision checks, fixed-obstacle/via guards, and reference DRC validation still gate publication. Rejected and protected routes retain their original vertices. A 1e-9 mm tolerance applies only when comparing residual clearances; splitting unchanged segments produced approximately 1e-15 mm round-off differences. New errors and meaningful clearance regressions remain rejected. Segment lengths use the scaled `getVectorLength` calculation suggested in [the review](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2769#discussion_r4135330518), following [high-density-repair01#24](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair01/pull/24). This replaces `Math.hypot`, whose platform-dependent rounding can change `Math.ceil(length / 0.5)` and therefore the number of inserted vertices. Scaling protects the calculation from overflow and underflow. The 0.5 mm subdivision spacing and 32-subdivision cap bound the refinement resolution and work; existing DRC clearance requirements remain unchanged. ### Visual example: opening a via-to-trace clearance gap These are close-ups of the actual `bugreport107-board-1726` solver outputs before and after the fix (macOS run), with the **same location, layer, and scale**. Blue shows bottom-layer copper. The red circle marks the central via's outer copper radius plus the required **0.1 mm clearance**; the neighboring trace's copper edge must stay outside it. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | | The trace just below and to the right of the central via enters the required clearance area. | The trace bends outward, opening the gap while the via stays in exactly the same place. | The solver inserts initially collinear points into eligible long spans, giving the existing repair solver places to bend locally. The candidate is accepted only after the collision and reference DRC checks described above. The dashed trace styling identifies the bottom layer; it does not represent physical breaks in the copper. This crop illustrates **one repaired gap**; the **97 → 89** reduction below is the total across the entire board. For `bugreport107-board-1726`, using the unchanged relaxed DRC preset: | Error category | Before | After | | --- | ---: | ---: | | Via-to-trace clearance | 43 | 36 | | Pad-to-trace clearance | 23 | 22 | | Trace overlap / clearance | 22 | 22 | | Via spacing | 9 | 9 | | **Total** | **97** | **89** | With the board's declared 0.25 mm via-hole clearance and board-edge checks, the final count improves from 132 to 124. The comparison found no new error identities, identical geometry for all 758 emitted vias, and unchanged IDs and endpoints for all 763 traces. There are still 89 relaxed DRC errors; this PR addresses the small clearance gaps that can be repaired without moving vias or terminals. Validation: - `tests/bugs/bugreport107-board-1726.test.ts` explicitly requires at most 89 final DRC errors, in addition to its existing stage-improvement and snapshot assertions. - 23 focused tests pass (288 assertions), including clearance projection, independent nudges, bounded regional repair, and vector-length precision at zero, the 0.5 mm subdivision boundary, and extreme magnitudes. The new synthetic straight-span regression demonstrates the failure without subdivision and successful repair with it, independently of bugreport107. - Junction-preservation coverage runs with subdivision both disabled and enabled; reference-validation coverage accepts floating-point round-off and rejects a 1e-7 mm regression. - Full macOS bugreport107 regression passes with the explicit 89-error ceiling (7 assertions). Full Linux x64 CI regression with Bun 1.3.8 passes the same numeric ceiling and the corrected snapshot, which comes from its inspected received SVG and reports 89 errors. Linux ARM runs with Bun 1.3.8 and 1.3.14 also produce 89 errors and identical geometry to one another, but a different route variant from x64. - All nine CI test shards pass on commit `984e694cd`, along with formatting, type checking, build, Vercel build, and the string-ID check. [Passing test run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/36569946508). - `bun run build` passes, including TypeScript declarations. - `git diff --check` passes.

title: Reduce bugreport107 DRC errors to 63 on macOS and 65 on Linux
description: Reduces DRC errors in bugreport107 from 82 to 63 on macOS and 65 on Linux by implementing a final whole-board clearance projection that moves wire bends and vias together.
body:
## Problem and fix

On bugreport107, the existing bounded repair reaches 82 DRC errors in the emitted board. It runs two partial clearance projections after regional search, but those passes deliberately keep vias fixed. The wire bends they improve can open room for a via to move, yet the solver stops before trying that coupled motion again.

Run one final whole-board clearance projection on the retained wire geometry, with the same 0.01 mm precision margin already used by the partial projections. This pass moves wire bends and vias together. It uses the existing fixed-obstacle and via-to-pad physical guards and is published only when the complete reference DRC has fewer errors. The via-to-pad guard compares the proposal with the immediately preceding routes: subdivision may add bend vertices, while the two wire-only passes keep every drill fixed. The bug-report assertion and both platform snapshots now reflect the resulting route.

On macOS, the full bugreport107 solve improves from **82 to 63 relaxed DRC errors** (19 fewer); Linux CI reports **65**. The macOS bounded-repair stage improves from 122 to 86. All 763 trace endpoint pairs remain fixed.

| DRC category (macOS) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Accidental copper-contact shorts (subset of trace errors) | 16 | 3 |
| All trace errors | 19 | 8 |
| Pad-to-trace clearance | 20 | 0 |
| Via-to-via clearance | 9 | 3 |
| Via-to-trace clearance | 34 | 52 |
| **Total** | **82** | **63** |

The via-to-trace category rises by 18 as the coupled solver relocates copper; the other categories fall by 37 combined. The complete-board DRC guard checks the net result, so this is a measured improvement, not a claim that every individual clearance improves.

body:
## Motivation

The crystal placement analyzer only evaluates crystals with exactly two source ports. Four-pin crystals also have two grounded case pins, so their load-capacitor placement is skipped even when the signal network should be analyzed.

## What this PR does

- Adds a focused Circuit JSON reproduction derived from a real USB hub board.
- Models Y2 as a `simple_crystal` with `pin_variant: "four_pin"` and renders the built-in four-pin crystal symbol.
- Preserves the 24 MHz frequency, 12 pF load capacitance, two signal pins, and two grounded case pins.
- Keeps only U13, Y2, R33, C31, and C32 so unrelated analyzer findings do not obscure the target behavior.
- Records the current bug: `CrystalLoadCapacitorPlacementSolver` reports zero `CrystalNotCenteredOverLoadCapacitors` issues.

This PR only adds the reproduction; it does not change the solver.

## References

- [Renesas 8V41NS0412 Evaluation Board User Guide, Figure 5 on page 10](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/mah/8v41ns0412-evaluation-board-user-guide) shows a four-pin crystal with pins 1 and 3 used for the oscillator signals, pins 2 and 4 grounded, and a load capacitor from each signal to ground.
- [Microchip USB2244 Hardware Design Checklist, section 6](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/UNG/ProductDocuments/DesignChecklist/USB2244-HW-Design-Checklist-00004319.pdf#page=8) documents the USB hub oscillator and load-capacitor network.

body:
Stacked on #126.

Adds `RelayFlybackDiodePlacementSolver`, reporting `FlybackDiodeSeparatedFromRelayCoil` when a local, label-connected protection diode is placed away from its relay coil. The real controller reports two findings: K1/D1 and K2/D2. Existing trace simplification does not report either pair.

Recognition requires named coil/contact pins, a diode across both coil nets, and a grounded-emitter transistor driver with the diode's anode at its collector. Nearby or directly wired loops, separate blocks, reversed polarity, shared coil pairs, and ambiguous placements are excluded. The advisory preserves polarity and pin assignments; it does not prescribe exact coordinates.

title: Reproduce 0.08 mm terminal neckdown from fragmented pad obstacles
description: Reproduces a bug where the terminal width calculation incorrectly reduces a valid trace width due to fragmented pad representation, without changing solver behavior.
body:
## Motivation

A single physical pad can be represented in SRJ as multiple adjacent rectangles sharing the same pad ID. The power trace expander currently calculates the terminal width using only one rectangle instead of the complete connected pad. This can unnecessarily reduce a valid `0.15 mm` trace to `0.08 mm`, creating a manufacturing-rule violation. This PR provides a minimal reproduction of that behavior.

## Issue

`PowerTraceClearanceRepairSolver` can create a terminal segment below `minTraceWidth` when one physical pad is represented by adjacent rectangular SRJ obstacles.

The endpoint-width calculation currently measures only the rectangle containing the terminal. In this reproduction, that rectangle is 0.10 mm tall and the terminal is 0.01 mm off its centerline, so the calculated limit is:

`2 × (0.05 - 0.01) = 0.08 mm`

`repairConnectedPadNeck` then applies that limit to a 0.30 mm-long terminal segment even though the configured minimum is 0.15 mm and the complete pad union has enough copper for it.

This is a general fragmented-pad problem, not a condition tied to one board or component. It can affect polygon, curved, annular, or other custom pads represented by multiple connected rectangles.

## Why this SRJ is valid

Core converts a non-axis-aligned polygon `pcb_smtpad` into 0.10 mm-tall rectangles with `fillPolygonWithRects`. Every generated rectangle retains the original `pcb_smtpad_id` in `connectedTo`: [Core obstacle conversion](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/main/lib/utils/obstacles/getObstaclesFromCircuitJson.ts#L197-L226).

The reduced fixture follows that contract directly:

- three adjacent 0.60 × 0.10 mm rectangles;
- every fragment shares `pcb_smtpad_fragmented` and the same `POWER` connection;
- their physical union is 0.60 × 0.30 mm;
- the terminal is at `(0, 0.01)`, so a 0.15 mm terminal spans `x = [-0.075, 0.075]` and `y = [-0.065, 0.085]`, entirely inside the union.

This keeps the reproduction at the power-trace-expander SRJ boundary. It does not depend on the acoustic-tuner TSX, its imported footprint, or the full autorouter pipeline. It is the reduced follow-up to the SRJ-origin concern raised on [tscircuit-autorouter#2638](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2638).

## Reproduced result

- Input minimum-width segment: `0.1500 mm`
- Output terminal segment: `0.0800 mm`
- Material below-minimum length: `0.299999 mm`
- `repairedPadNeckSegmentCount`: `1`
- Solver result: complete, not failed

The three labeled gray rows are adjacent SRJ rectangles that represent one physical pad. Both panels show the same terminal and the same local pad geometry. The left panel shows the expected 0.15 mm segment fitting across the complete pad, while the right panel shows the expander's 0.08 mm output in red.

![Fragmented pad terminal neckdown reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/power-trace-expander/3760cc2/tests/__snapshots__/fragmented-connected-pad-neckdown.snap.svg)

## Expected

Terminal-width calculation should consider the complete connected physical pad, rather than one rectangular fragment, before reducing a segment below `minTraceWidth`. A genuinely narrow pad may still require an explicit terminal neckdown; this case is different because the full same-pad union supports 0.15 mm.

This PR is reproduction-only and does not change solver behavior.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 86 pass, 0 fail, 2,885 assertions
- focused reproduction and fixture-catalog tests — 2 pass, 0 fail, 33 assertions
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run build` — pass
- Biome formatting for every changed TypeScript/TSX file — pass
- `git diff --check` — pass
- generated SVG rendered and visually inspected

The repository-wide `bun run format:check` still reports pre-existing formatting differences in `tests/alias-cache-lifetime.test.ts`, `tests/disallow-new-vias.test.ts`, `tests/grid-route-cost-pruning.test.ts`, and `tests/shared-alias-cache.test.ts`. None is changed here.

The PR targets `fix/enforce-connectivity-monotonicity`, the active power-expander line pinned by the autorouter, rather than the older default branch.

title: Resolve selected schematic variant parameters
description: Resolves schematic parameters based on the selected project variant, ensuring that variant-specific parameters are correctly prioritized and rendered without leaking values from other variants.
body:
## Summary

- keep base project parameters and each project variant in separate cached scopes
- add explicit `variantName` selection to schematic parameter resolution and SVG rendering
- resolve indexed Altium sections such as `Parameter2_1` only for their owning variant
- apply Altium precedence: project, then document, then selected variant
- preserve the lower-priority value when a higher-priority scope uses Altium's `*` inheritance marker
- resolve the built-in `=VariantName` string from the explicit selection

## Root cause

The original change treated every `Parameter<number>_<number>` section as a project-global parameter. Those sections are variant-owned: Altium reserves parameter owner 1 for the base project, so `ProjectVariant1` owns `Parameter2_*`, `ProjectVariant2` owns `Parameter3_*`, and so on. Loading all of them into one map leaked the last variant into renders that had not selected any variant.

The official TI LMX2694 project demonstrates both scopes: variant `001` resolves `EVM_Orderable` to `LMX2694EPEVM`, while variant `002` resolves it to `LMX2694SEPEVM`.

Altium documents variant parameters as higher priority than schematic-document and project parameters, and documents `*` as explicitly inheriting the next lower-priority value: https://www.altium.com/documentation/knowledge-base/altium-designer/reduce-repetitive-documentation-tasks-with-parameterized-project-template

## Regression coverage

- no selected variant does not import variant-owned parameters
- two selected variants resolve their own values without leaking
- selected variant parameters override document and project parameters
- `*` in the selected variant inherits the document value
- `*` in the document inherits the project value
- SVG rendering forwards the selected variant
- `=VariantName` resolves from the explicit selection

## Verification

- `bun test` — 346 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- verified against the real TI LMX2694 two-variant project

title: fix : copper polygons and their cutouts
description: Fixes the issue where copper geometry is lost in polygon-cutout cases, ensuring linked cutouts are retained and properly exported as BREP inner rings.
body: ## Motivation The converter loses copper geometry in two polygon-cutout cases. A linked cutout can suppress a polygon with no poured-copper region. On the [MIT-licensed CH582 board](https://github.com/iot-lorawan/CH582_PCB_SCH/blob/b65bce802295c6c40413c5bc3ea54682820619c1/PCB_ch582_2022-06-16.pcbdoc), two polygons survive, but their four unlinked cutouts are missing from the exported pours. # Reference ## Changes - Suppress a polygon only when a linked `COPPER` region supplies its poured geometry; retain linked cutouts as inner rings. - Resolve linked polygon references by record, including explicit IDs; dangling references do not become inferred holes. - Match unlinked, fully enclosed cutouts to polygons by copper layer and contour geometry, then export those cutouts as BREP inner rings. Cutouts that are not fully enclosed are not inferred as holes. - Reject boundary-touching cutouts as BREP inner holes, with concave-polygon and fractional-mil regressions. - Subtract the combined cutout geometry with `polygon-clipping` before emitting copper. Overlapping and duplicate cutouts remain empty, and a copper island is clipped if another cutout covers it; all three cases have regressions. - Check cutouts on both CH582 copper layers, with a bottom-copper snapshot and an all-layer PCB snapshot. The Circuit JSON renderings show the cutout openings. - Assert that CH582 bottom-layer tracks also survive conversion as Circuit JSON traces. - Keep the small linked-cutout regression and the check that poured-copper regions do not duplicate polygons. [CH582 before, bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/altium-to-circuit-json/2d855de/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts.snap.svg) · [after, bottom copper](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/8d11a62e391957c94146f762f624472606c69cb0/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts.snap.svg) · [after, all-layer PCB](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/altium-to-circuit-json/8d11a62e391957c94146f762f624472606c69cb0/tests/svg/__snapshots__/ch582-polygon-cutouts-board.snap.svg) The source panels are rendered by `altiumts`, not Altium's official viewer. The Circuit JSON panels use `circuit-to-svg`, which [masks trace strokes covered by a finalized pour](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/blob/main/lib/pcb/copper-pour-trace-mask.ts). That is why bottom routes visible in the source panel are not visible in the rendered Circuit JSON panel; they are present in the converted Circuit JSON. The pre-fix reproduction was merged in #95.

title: Preserve rich line and arc component bodies

The new predicate requires at least three body primitives across at least two primitive kinds. This keeps sparse decoration on the generic-box path without requiring one arbitrary combination of shapes.

description: Preserves custom single-input triangular gate bodies instead of degrading them to generic boxes, keeps primitive gate pins, inversion bubbles, clock markers, active-low overbars, and source font sizing aligned with the imported geometry, normalizes only numeric multipart prefixes for gate classification, while retaining original labels such as 1A, 1Y, 2A, and 2Y, preserves both the two-input and Schmitt-trigger gate bodies in TI LMG342X-BB-EVM; power-only multipart sections remain ordinary boxes, includes focused semantic tests and side-by-side AltiumCircuit JSON SVG regressions.
body:
## Summary

- preserve custom single-input triangular gate bodies instead of degrading them to generic boxes
- keep primitive gate pins, inversion bubbles, clock markers, active-low overbars, and source font sizing aligned with the imported geometry
- normalize only numeric multipart prefixes for gate classification, while retaining original labels such as `1A`, `1Y`, `2A`, and `2Y`
- preserve both the two-input and Schmitt-trigger gate bodies in TI LMG342X-BB-EVM; power-only multipart sections remain ordinary boxes
- include focused semantic tests and side-by-side Altium/Circuit JSON SVG regressions

## Root cause

Gate recognition expected literal `A`, `B`, and `Y` pin names. Multipart Altium libraries prefix those functional names with their part number (`1A`, `1Y`, and so on), so valid gate primitives were ignored. Single-input triangular gates also required a dedicated primitive rendering path to keep pin-edge graphics and source labels attached.

The classifier now removes a leading numeric part prefix only while deciding gate semantics. It never rewrites the source port label.

## Verification

- `bun test ./tests/conversion` — 148 pass, 1,719 assertions

- `bun run build`

title: Fix Altium PCB dimension axes in TI EVM imports
description: Fixes incorrect PCB dimension measurements by projecting Altium linear dimensions onto their stored ANGLE axis, ensuring accurate rendering and reference points in TI EVM imports.
body:
## Summary

- project Altium linear dimensions onto their stored `ANGLE` axis instead of measuring the diagonal between reference points
- preserve the original second reference anchor with a fabrication-note extension path to the projected measurement endpoint
- derive the axis with `transformation-matrix`, following the repository and handbook convention for rotations
- render solder mask and drill openings in the four newly added TI EVM comparison snapshots so uncovered substrate is not presented as missing board geometry
- refresh the five existing TI PMP snapshots that exercise the corrected dimension behavior

## Root cause

Altium linear dimensions may store reference points that differ along both axes while `ANGLE` identifies the actual measurement axis. Measuring the direct distance between the references produced diagonal dimensions and incorrect labels. Projecting the second endpoint fixed the measurement but discarded where its extension line originated, so the rendered line no longer reached the feature being measured.

The converter now computes the projection once and uses it for both the Circuit JSON dimension and, when the second reference is off-axis, a fabrication-note path from the original anchor to the projected endpoint. Already aligned dimensions do not receive an extra path.

## Verification

- handbook compliance and one-top-level-function source-structure tests
- four focused PCB-dimension conversion tests, including an off-axis second reference and its extension path
- nine TI EVM PCB SVG snapshot tests covering changed and unchanged dimension cases

Circuit JSON now produces a single GPIO SysConfig document for **AM2434BSDFHIALVR**. A source-port ball alias A7 fixes the output to MCU_GPIO0_5; changing that alias to B7 fixes it to MCU_GPIO0_6. Unknown parts, ambiguous identities, ownership errors, and unsupported active functions fail explicitly.

### Implementation

- Public `CircuitJsonToSysConfigConverter` with three concrete stages: resolve MCU/target, validate GPIO, construct the document. `step()` performs one stage; `runUntilFinished()` completes the remaining stages; `getOutput()` rejects unfinished conversion. Failed stages do not advance, completed steps do not duplicate output, and inputs are snapshotted.
- The convenience function is a thin wrapper over the same converter. Shared context carries the selected component/port, resolved target/request, and document; the GPIO resolver uses that resolved target.
